runs.text: 1. What is a Design Pattern?
A design pattern is a set of rules or a proven solution for a frequently occurring problem. It provides a standard way of solving a problem, but it is not itself an implementation.
For example, when a requirement is to restrict a class to only one object, the Singleton Design Pattern provides a standard solution.
2. What is the Singleton Design Pattern?
Singleton Design Pattern is a design pattern used to restrict the number of objects created for a class to one.
Multiple parts of an application can hold references to the same object, but only one object is created.
3. Why do we need to restrict object creation to one?
Some entities or resources logically require only one object to represent them.

For example, if a class represents a Prime Minister, creating multiple Prime Minister objects does not represent the intended requirement. The requirement is to create one object and allow different references to access that same object.
4. What happens when an object is created using new?
When an object is created using new, a new object is created in memory.

When an object is printed using

6. How can object creation be restricted from an outside class?
The outside class must not be allowed to directly call the constructor.
The constructor is made private.

7. Why is the constructor made private in Singleton Design Pattern?
The constructor is made private so that an outside class cannot directly create an object using new.
This keeps object creation under the control of the Singleton class.
8. If the constructor is private, how can the object be created?
The object can be created from inside the same class because the private constructor is accessible within that class.
The class provides a public method through which an outside class can request the object.
The method returns the object reference instead of allowing the outside class to directly call the constructor.

10. Why should the Singleton method be static?
The outside class needs to call the method without creating an object first.
Therefore, the method is made static.

blocks.text: PrimeMinister pm = PrimeMinister.getPrimeMinister();

runs.text: The method can be called using the class name.
If the method were not static, an object would be required to call it. But creating the object itself is restricted by the private constructor.
11. Why should the reference variable be static?
If a static method needs to access the reference variable, the reference variable should also be static.
A static method cannot directly access a non-static instance variable.
Therefore:

blocks.text: private static PrimeMinister ref;

runs.text: is used instead of:

blocks.text: private PrimeMinister ref;

runs.text: 12. Why is the reference variable initialized with null?
The reference variable is used to determine whether an object has already been created.
Initially, no object exists, so the reference contains null.

blocks.text: private static PrimeMinister ref = null;

runs.text: The method checks:

blocks.text: if (ref == null)

runs.text: If ref is null, the object has not yet been created, so a new object is created.
If ref is not null, an object already exists, so the existing reference is returned.
13. What is the complete logic of the Singleton Design Pattern?
The Singleton implementation follows these steps:
Make the constructor private.
Create a private static reference variable.
Create a public static method that returns the object reference.
Check whether the reference is null.
If the reference is null, create the object.
If the reference is not null, return the existing reference.
The object can be accessed from another class:
Only one object is created. Both
modi
and up refer to the same object.
14. If the Singleton method is called 10 times, how many objects are created?
Only one object is created.
During the first call:
ref == null
is true, so the object is created.
After that, ref contains the object reference. Every subsequent call finds that ref is not null and returns the existing reference.
All three references point to the same object.
15. Can one object have multiple reference variables?
Yes.
One object can have multiple reference variables.

blocks.text:
PrimeMinister p1 = PrimeMinister.getPrimeMinister();
PrimeMinister p2 = PrimeMinister.getPrimeMinister();

runs.text: Here, p1 and p2 are different reference variables, but both refer to the same object.
Number of objects = 1
Number of references = 2
The number of references can increase without creating additional objects.
16. What happens if the Singleton condition ref == null is not checked?
If the condition is not checked and the method creates a new object every time, every method call can create another object.
If this method is called 10 times, 10 objects can be created.
Therefore, the null check is required to restrict object creation to one.
17. Why should the reference variable be private?
The reference variable should be private so that an outside class cannot directly access or modify it.

blocks.text: private static PrimeMinister ref;

runs.text: Keeping it private ensures that object creation and reference management remain controlled by the Singleton class.
18. What happens if the reference variable is public instead of private?
The outside class could directly access the reference variable.
This would allow outside code to interfere with the reference and potentially change its value.
Therefore, the reference variable should be private.
19. What happens if the Singleton constructor is not private?
If the constructor is accessible from outside the class, an external class can directly use new.

blocks.text:
PrimeMinister pm1 = new PrimeMinister();
PrimeMinister pm2 = new PrimeMinister();

runs.text: This allows multiple objects to be created and breaks the Singleton requirement.
Therefore, the constructor must be private.
20. What happens if the Singleton method is not public?
If the method is not accessible from outside the class, the outside class cannot call it.
The method provides controlled access to the Singleton object, so it should be public.
The standard combination is:

blocks.text:
private constructor
private static reference
public static method

runs.text: 21. What happens if the Singleton method is not static?
The method would require an object to call it.
However, the constructor is private, so the outside class cannot create the object required to call the method.
Therefore, the method must be static.

1. Private constructor
2. Private static reference variable
3. Public static method that returns the object reference
The method creates the object only when the reference is null. If the object already exists, the existing reference is returned.

30. What is inheritance?
Inheritance is the process of acquiring the properties and
behaviors
of one entity into another entity.
From the class perspective, it means acquiring properties and
behaviors
from one class into another class.
The concept can be understood as:
One entity → Another entity
One class → Another class
One object → Another object
31. Why is inheritance required?
The primary advantage of inheritance is code reusability.
If common properties and
behaviors
have already been implemented in one class, another class can inherit them instead of rewriting the same code.
This reduces development time because existing code is reused.

behaviors
